title: Enhancement: test_cont_link_flap is flaky due to using a sleep to wait for memory stable
author: peterbailey-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the enhancement

The test should wait intelligently until memory stable instead of arbitrary 30 seconds

### Current Behavior

The test does this:
`        # Wait 30s for the memory usage to be stable`
but on topos with more routes this is inelegant and can be flaky.

### Proposed Behavior

use wait_until to verify memory stability, allow more time on T2 topos.

comments.author: yxieca
comments.body:
**AI review — Changes requested**

### Blocking

1. `wait_until(wait_timeout, 5, 5, self.check_frr_daemon_memory_stable, duthost, memory_usages)` — the argument shape needs confirmation against the sibling `wait_until` calls in this same file. Anchor: the new call site in `check_continuous_link_flap` (test_cont_link_flap.py, ~line 223). Under the `wait_until(timeout, interval, delay, condition, *args)` signature, the third positional `5` is a 5s initial delay; if the pattern being copied is actually the 3-arg `wait_until(timeout, interval, predicate, ...)` form, this is an off-by-one-arg copy-paste that both burns 5s per run and shifts every subsequent positional. Either confirm the leading `delay=5` is intentional (and add a one-line "why", per the constant-justification convention) or drop it. Note: two core models read this same call as `(timeout, interval=5, delay=5)` and treated it as benign — the disagreement between passes is exactly why this needs an author confirmation rather than a silent approve.

2. Warn-and-proceed on non-stabilization weakens the assertion this test exists to make. Anchor: `if not wait_until(...): logging.warning("FRR daemon memory did not stabilize within {}s, proceeding to check")` (test_cont_link_flap.py, ~line 224). Versus the old unconditional `sleep(30)`, this is a behavior change where a genuinely-unstable FRR memory condition — the leak signal in a link-flap test — becomes a non-fatal `warning` and the test proceeds anyway. This is a loosening; it needs a written "why" in the PR body, and the failure detail must be preserved: today the per-daemon/per-asic deltas are logged at `logging.debug` (~line 86) while the outer message is `logging.warning`, so when it fires the diagnostic explaining *which* asic/daemon was unstable is suppressed at default log level. Promote the inner log to `info`/`warning` (or fold the collected deltas into the outer message), and either fail the test or record the last-observed deltas so the regression class stays catchable.

### Grounded nits

- `check_frr_daemon_memory_stable` mutates its caller-owned `memory_usages` dict in place (`prev_usages_per_asic[daemon] = current_usage`, ~line 89) while serving as the `wait_until` predicate. This is *necessary* for each poll to compare against the previous poll rather than the initial snapshot, but a function named `check_...` reads as pure. Add a one-line comment documenting the in-place update, or rename to advertise the state mutation — per the repo convention that boolean helpers read as predicates.
- `prev_mem == 0` forces `change_percent = float('inf')`, permanently marking that daemon unstable even if `curr_mem == 0` too (test_cont_link_flap.py, ~line 83). If a zero reading from `get_frr_daemon_memory_usage` is ever legitimate/transient, the loop can never converge and will chew the full budget before warning. Treat `prev_mem == 0 and curr_mem == 0` as stable, or skip that cycle.
- `threshold_percent=1` is an unexplained magic default (~line 73). A short comment or module-level constant (alongside the 60/30 timeout) would help the next person tuning T2 behavior.
- Minor: the `logging.debug(...)` continuation (~line 86) is indented deeper than its opening call, and the diff mixes lazy-`%` logging with `.format()` in the adjacent warning — a `flake8`/`black` pass (house line length 120) would normalize both.

---

comments.author: peterbailey-arista
comments.body:
@yxieca 
1. Yes this is intentional, we are checking for stability as opposed to blindly sleeping for 30 seconds. To do this safely we need a minimal initial delay that will ensure the first memory check takes 5 sseconds after the the initial memory usage sampling.
2. This is incorrect, there is no assertion weakening introduced by my PR. My change is strictly better in that it provides a warning and then proceeds on with the original verification which may still pass whereas the original code waited 30 seconds and then did the same. Promoting this debug log would be noisy, every daemon for every wait_until iteration should not necessitate a print saying it is not yet stable. The final assert will specify the daemons that fail if there is a real problem.

Non blocking nits:
1. this is a recurring pattern in the codebase. See `get_crm_resources`, `check_stabilized` wait_until usages which mutate resources owned by their callers.
2. memory is measured at the granularity of bytes, if the memory is 0 then the daemon is not running and we do not want to consider this as "stable"
3. Admittedly threshold_percent is simply a number that works experimentally. It just had to be more strict than the 5 or 10% used by the actual assertion to ensure stability was not realized too early.
